pathway.title: Science Applications International Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Cash flow is durable because most revenue is cost-reimbursed and capital needs are light. Cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue and capital expenditure is 0.44% of revenue, so fiscal 2026 free cash flow of USD 577 million was 85.36% of reported EBITDA and last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt. Fiscal 2026 cash flow was helped by receivables collections of USD 161 million and cash taxes of USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, so it should not be extrapolated. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 93, 129; calculation F05; calculation F04; calculation F18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Revenue visibility is thinner than the backlog suggests. Backlog is USD 22,136 million, or 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, but only 17.25% is funded, net bookings were 0.87 times revenue in the first half after 1.07 times in fiscal 2026, and revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 before growing 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027, of which about 2.9% was organic. Funding lapses and contract reviews are the channel through which unfunded backlog turns into lost or delayed revenue. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24, 27, 34; calculation F05; calculation F10; calculation F07; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings momentum is real but slowing, which corrects the weight Financial foundation puts on first-half growth. Reported EBITDA rose 24.02% in the first half, but the gain was front-loaded: it rose 41.03% in the first quarter and 9.04% in the second, when adjusted EBITDA rose 4.32% and its margin slipped to 10.3% from 10.5% despite organic revenue growth of about 5.3%. The first half also includes a USD 12 million gain on the sale of an investment that the adjusted measure does not remove; without it adjusted EBITDA growth is 17.84%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 27, 31; calculation F02; calculation F06; calculation F07; calculation F09; calculation F08; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is moderate on the issuer's own definitions but is set by shareholder returns. Gross debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA is 3.29x, 3.18x on adjusted EBITDA and 3.12x net, or 3.14x net pro forma for the USD 15.5 million dividend payable on 2026-10-23; net debt is USD 2,359 million, or USD 2,374.5 million pro forma. Returns of USD 515 million took 89.25% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and, with the USD 203 million acquisition, exceeded it, and returns of USD 319 million were 128.11% of free cash flow in the first half of fiscal 2027, lifting net debt by USD 141 million and USD 54 million; each further USD 100 million of net debt adds 0.13x. This corrects the operating map in Business & governance, which says returns exceeded free cash flow in both periods: on their own they did so only in the first half of fiscal 2027. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93; calculation F01; calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation F17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable until the notes due April 2028. Liquidity is USD 1,126 million, mostly the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver, before the dividend payable on 2026-10-23 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established, and it covers the USD 48 million of maturities through fiscal 2028 23.46 times; USD 489 million falls due in fiscal 2029, mostly the USD 400 million notes. Term loan amortisation rises from USD 27.50 million to USD 82.50 million a year from late 2028, and 63.99% of principal floats after the interest rate swaps expired, so 50 bp costs about USD 8 million a year. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 132, 135; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F03; calculation F16; calculation F13; calculation F14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Event risk sits in the antitrust investigation, federal funding and contract reviews. The company cannot estimate fines or penalties in the investigation, the Department of Homeland Security was shut down from February to April 2026, and agencies are reviewing contracts, although the company reports no material financial effect so far. Governance does not offset these risks: there is no sponsor, the credit agreement may limit dividends and buybacks only at leverage ratios that are not printed, and governance risk is Medium. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 23, 24; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation F05; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The first strength is cash-flow durability: cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue and capital expenditure is 0.44% of revenue, so most cost increases are passed through and free cash flow of USD 577 million covered debt service in fiscal 2026. The second is liquidity and maturity shape: USD 1,126 million of liquidity against USD 48 million of maturities through fiscal 2028 means no refinancing is needed before the notes due April 2028. The third is customer longevity: several relationships of 20 years or more and a USD 22,136 million backlog support renewal of work. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 93, 115; calculation F05; calculation F03; calculation F16; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is shareholder returns that absorb free cash flow, 89.25% in fiscal 2026 and 128.11% in the first half of fiscal 2027, which with the acquisition lifted net debt by USD 141 million and USD 54 million with no sponsor or covenant ratio to restrain them. The second is dependence on one buyer, with 52.02% of revenue from the Department of War and 17.25% of backlog funded, so a funding or contract-review shock cuts volume. The third is fading momentum: second-quarter adjusted EBITDA rose 4.32% against 24.02% reported for the half, and net bookings were 0.87 times revenue. The fourth is an unquantified antitrust investigation and floating-rate exposure of 63.99% of principal. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 31, 34; calculation F04; calculation F05; calculation F06; calculation F10; calculation F13; calculation F02; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The filings state no sponsor, buyout, recapitalisation or pending acquisition financing. The transactions that matter to creditors are the September 2025 refinancing and the SilverEdge acquisition that followed it. On 2025-09-25 the company issued USD 500 million of unsecured senior notes due November 2033 and used the proceeds to repay the revolver due June 2027; on 2025-09-30 it replaced its 2027 term loan A and revolver with a USD 1,100 million term loan A and a USD 1,000 million revolver, both due September 2030; and on 2025-10-15 it acquired SilverEdge for a preliminary USD 203 million net of USD 6 million cash acquired, funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 116, 132, 134

After the quarter end, on 2026-08-14 the receivables purchase facility limit was raised from USD 300 million to USD 400 million, and on 2026-08-27 a quarterly dividend of USD 0.37 per share was declared, payable 2026-10-23. No later debt issue is stated, and the executed debt documents are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 20; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.value: Financial foundation for Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the consolidated registrant's statements, debt, liquidity and credit ratios from fiscal 2024 to the quarter ended 2026-07-31, with the last twelve months built from the 2026 annual report and the fiscal 2027 quarterly reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SAIC's reported leverage is 3.29x gross and 3.12x net on last-twelve-months EBITDA at July 31, 2026, and fiscal 2026 cash interest cover was 6.69x; these are accounting ratios, not the covenant test, whose headroom cannot be established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross leverage rose from 2.36x in fiscal 2024 mainly because that year's reported EBITDA included a USD 240 million divestiture gain; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA it was 3.14x then and is 3.18x now. Net debt rose by USD 54 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 because shareholder returns of USD 319 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 249 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 31; calculation C09; calculation C20; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has moved less than the reported series suggests. Gross debt over reported EBITDA was 2.36x at fiscal 2024, 3.14x at fiscal 2025, 3.68x at fiscal 2026 and 3.29x on the last twelve months to July 31, 2026, while gross debt over issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 3.14x, 3.13x, 3.51x and 3.18x. The fiscal 2024 reported figure is flattered by the divestiture gain, and the fiscal 2026 peak reflects both lower EBITDA, down from USD 708 million to USD 676 million, and higher debt after a year in which the company borrowed USD 271 million net, paid USD 203 million for the SilverEdge acquisition and returned USD 515 million to shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 93, 131; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14; calculation C10; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is strong but leans on items that can reverse. Operating cash flow was USD 609 million in fiscal 2026 and free cash flow USD 577 million, or 85.36% of reported EBITDA, yet cash taxes paid were USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, and collections of receivables added USD 161 million. Sales of receivables sit inside operating cash flow, so a smaller facility balance lowers it, as when the facility cut operating cash flow by USD 41 million in fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 129, 136; calculation C09; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns, not operations, are what lift net debt. In fiscal 2026 buybacks and dividends of USD 515 million and the USD 203 million acquisition exceeded free cash flow, and net debt rose by USD 141 million; in the first half of fiscal 2027 returns of USD 319 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 249 million, taking net debt to USD 2,359 million.

fields.value: Near-term liquidity and maturities are not pressing. Unrestricted cash is USD 126 million and the USD 1,000 million revolver due September 2030 is undrawn, so committed resources are USD 1,126 million before USD 8 million of letters of credit whose facility the filings do not name; scheduled maturities are USD 48 million through fiscal 2028 and USD 489 million in fiscal 2029, mostly the notes due April 2028.

fields.value: Definitions flatter leverage and cover. EBITDA adds back interest and the loss on sold receivables of USD 140 million in fiscal 2026 against interest expense of USD 128 million, so USD 12 million of receivables financing cost is left out of EBITDA, and USD 120 million of sold receivables at July 31, 2026 stay outside debt. Cash interest of USD 101 million is below the USD 128 million expense, which lifts cash cover.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that last-twelve-months gross leverage of 3.29x is below the 3.68x of fiscal 2026, that the USD 1,000 million revolver is undrawn and that maturities are small until fiscal 2029. It would win if first-half reported EBITDA growth of 24.02% persists and free cash flow again covers shareholder returns.

fields.value: The evidence for concern is that net debt has risen in every period since fiscal 2024, that revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 and that 98% of revenue comes from one customer, the U.S. government. A fall in federal funding, or an adverse result in the Department of Justice investigation, which the company says it cannot estimate, would change the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SAIC is a listed, mostly cost-reimbursed U.S. government contractor with no sponsor identified, so creditors depend on contract cash flows and board restraint rather than outside support, and shareholder returns took 89.25% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 79, 82, 93; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is almost wholly federal, 98% in fiscal 2026 and 52.02% from the Department of War, and USD 22,136 million of backlog at July 31, 2026 gives visibility, but only USD 3,818 million of it is funded. A criminal antitrust investigation is open with no estimate of penalties, the chief executive changed in October 2025, and a funding lapse or contract review would hit volume directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor stands behind the debt, and none is drawing value out of it. The filings name no parent, sponsor or controlling holder; the shares are listed on Nasdaq and held by about seventeen thousand holders of record, so there is no sponsor support to count on and no sponsor-led recapitalisation to fear. Holdings of large stockholders sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so concentration among them is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is very high but cushioned by contract type. Federal customers supply 98% of revenue and cost-reimbursement contracts supply 61.76% against 15.75% for firm-fixed-price work, so most cost increases are passed through to the customer while volume depends on appropriations: the Department of Homeland Security was shut down from February to April 2026, and open audits by the government's cost auditor can still disallow billed costs. The mechanism that matters for creditors is lost or delayed volume, not margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Backlog gives visibility, but little of it is funded and it is not growing. Total backlog was USD 22,136 million at July 31, 2026 against USD 22,622 million at January 30, 2026, only USD 3,818 million of it, or 17.25%, is funded, and net bookings of about USD 3.3 billion in the half were 0.87 times revenue. Remaining performance obligations are USD 6.4 billion, of which 75% is expected within twelve months, so most of the backlog still needs later funding or the exercise of options before it becomes revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 34; calculation A09; calculation A10; calculation A13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have priority over deleveraging. Buybacks and dividends of USD 515 million took 89.25% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow of USD 577 million and, with the USD 203 million SilverEdge acquisition, exceeded it by USD 141 million; in the first half of fiscal 2027 returns of USD 319 million were 128.11% of free cash flow of USD 249 million. The dividend of USD 0.37 per share each quarter is small beside the buyback, which the board authorised up to USD 1,200 million in December 2024, so returns can be cut quickly, but the filings do not commit the board to do so and say only that dividends and buybacks may be limited at certain leverage ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leadership and structure changed together, which raises execution risk in a period when revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 and grew 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027. The chief executive and other executives left in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, an interim chief executive served from October 2025 until February 2026, executive transition costs of USD 16 million net were added back in adjusted EBITDA, and five business groups were consolidated into three from 2026-01-31 with both reportable segments unchanged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: An open criminal antitrust investigation is the main unquantified claim. The company received federal grand jury subpoenas in April 2022 and October 2023, is producing documents and says it cannot estimate fines or penalties; separately it warns that adverse findings in government investigations and audits can lead to suspension or debarment, which for a business with 98% federal revenue would threaten most of its revenue if it occurred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a more benign view is that several customer relationships have lasted 20 years or more, that 61.76% of revenue is cost-reimbursed, that backlog is 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, and that returns to shareholders are discretionary, so the board could retain cash quickly. The view would move toward benign if returns fell back below free cash flow for several quarters and the investigation closed without a penalty.

fields.value: It would move toward cautious if revenue fell again after the 2.90% decline of fiscal 2026, if returns again exceeded free cash flow while net debt rose, or if a penalty, a debarment proceeding or a funding lapse longer than the 2026 shutdown appeared. The first-half revenue growth of 3.84% is partly acquired, since SilverEdge added USD 39 million, and the company puts growth excluding acquisitions at about 2.9%, so it does not by itself show recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings state no sponsor, buyout, recapitalisation or pending acquisition financing. The transactions that matter to creditors are the September 2025 refinancing and the SilverEdge acquisition that followed it. On 2025-09-25 the company issued USD 500 million of unsecured senior notes due November 2033 and used the proceeds to repay the revolver due June 2027; on 2025-09-30 it replaced its 2027 term loan A and revolver with a USD 1,100 million term loan A and a USD 1,000 million revolver, both due September 2030; and on 2025-10-15 it acquired SilverEdge for a preliminary USD 203 million net of USD 6 million cash acquired, funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the quarter end, on 2026-08-14 the receivables purchase facility limit was raised from USD 300 million to USD 400 million, and on 2026-08-27 a quarterly dividend of USD 0.37 per share was declared, payable 2026-10-23. No later debt issue is stated, and the executed debt documents are not supplied.

fields.value: The risk level is Medium because shareholder returns that exceeded free cash flow lift net debt with no sponsor or equity support to offset them, which implies a thinner creditor cushion if earnings fall. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, clean audit opinions, regular quarterly reporting and discretionary returns that the board can cut. Further analysis needs the proxy statement, the credit agreement and any later filing.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Science Applications International Corp (saic-1571123), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: business quality, earnings, cash flow, leverage, liquidity, governance and downside, drawn from the four filings to the quarter ended 2026-07-31 and the accepted Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules; no earlier run of this pathway exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SAIC is an adequate credit: cost-reimbursed federal contracts and light capital needs give free cash flow, but shareholder returns that absorb most of it, a mostly unfunded backlog and one dominant customer cap it, leaving gross leverage at 3.29x and net debt rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 115; calculation F01; calculation F04; calculation F05; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns, not operations, set the leverage path, and the first-half earnings surge is fading, with second-quarter adjusted EBITDA up only 4.32%. The main downside is a federal funding or contract-review shock that cuts volume while returns keep lifting net debt; no covenant ratio is reported, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24, 31; calculation F06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is durable because most revenue is cost-reimbursed and capital needs are light. Cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue and capital expenditure is 0.44% of revenue, so fiscal 2026 free cash flow of USD 577 million was 85.36% of reported EBITDA and last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt. Fiscal 2026 cash flow was helped by receivables collections of USD 161 million and cash taxes of USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, so it should not be extrapolated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 93, 129; calculation F05; calculation F04; calculation F18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue visibility is thinner than the backlog suggests. Backlog is USD 22,136 million, or 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, but only 17.25% is funded, net bookings were 0.87 times revenue in the first half after 1.07 times in fiscal 2026, and revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 before growing 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027, of which about 2.9% was organic. Funding lapses and contract reviews are the channel through which unfunded backlog turns into lost or delayed revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 24, 27, 34; calculation F05; calculation F10; calculation F07; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings momentum is real but slowing, which corrects the weight Financial foundation puts on first-half growth. Reported EBITDA rose 24.02% in the first half, but the gain was front-loaded: it rose 41.03% in the first quarter and 9.04% in the second, when adjusted EBITDA rose 4.32% and its margin slipped to 10.3% from 10.5% despite organic revenue growth of about 5.3%. The first half also includes a USD 12 million gain on the sale of an investment that the adjusted measure does not remove; without it adjusted EBITDA growth is 17.84%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 27, 31; calculation F02; calculation F06; calculation F07; calculation F09; calculation F08; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate on the issuer's own definitions but is set by shareholder returns. Gross debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA is 3.29x, 3.18x on adjusted EBITDA and 3.12x net, or 3.14x net pro forma for the USD 15.5 million dividend payable on 2026-10-23; net debt is USD 2,359 million, or USD 2,374.5 million pro forma. Returns of USD 515 million took 89.25% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and, with the USD 203 million acquisition, exceeded it, and returns of USD 319 million were 128.11% of free cash flow in the first half of fiscal 2027, lifting net debt by USD 141 million and USD 54 million; each further USD 100 million of net debt adds 0.13x. This corrects the operating map in Business & governance, which says returns exceeded free cash flow in both periods: on their own they did so only in the first half of fiscal 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are comfortable until the notes due April 2028. Liquidity is USD 1,126 million, mostly the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver, before the dividend payable on 2026-10-23 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established, and it covers the USD 48 million of maturities through fiscal 2028 23.46 times; USD 489 million falls due in fiscal 2029, mostly the USD 400 million notes. Term loan amortisation rises from USD 27.50 million to USD 82.50 million a year from late 2028, and 63.99% of principal floats after the interest rate swaps expired, so 50 bp costs about USD 8 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 132, 135; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F03; calculation F16; calculation F13; calculation F14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Event risk sits in the antitrust investigation, federal funding and contract reviews. The company cannot estimate fines or penalties in the investigation, the Department of Homeland Security was shut down from February to April 2026, and agencies are reviewing contracts, although the company reports no material financial effect so far. Governance does not offset these risks: there is no sponsor, the credit agreement may limit dividends and buybacks only at leverage ratios that are not printed, and governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 23, 24; 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation F05; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that adjusted leverage has stayed between 3.13x and 3.51x over four periods, that last-twelve-months gross leverage of 3.29x is below the 3.68x of fiscal 2026, that the revolver is undrawn and that returns are discretionary. A board that kept returns below free cash flow for several quarters, with the investigation closed without a penalty, would justify a stronger view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F01; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A weaker view would follow if adjusted EBITDA growth stayed near the 4.32% of the second quarter, if net bookings stayed below revenue, if a funding lapse lasted longer than the 2026 shutdown, or if the investigation ended in a penalty or a debarment proceeding. Falling back to the fiscal 2026 EBITDA level would put gross leverage at 3.68x, and that is the level the company has already lived with, so the view turns on earnings momentum and the board's payout choices, not on liquidity.

fields.value: SAIC sells technical, engineering and IT services almost entirely to the U.S. government: 98% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 97% in the first half of fiscal 2027, with the Department of War alone at 52.02%. Customer relationships include several of 20 years or more, and cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue, so cash flow is visible and cost-protected, but it depends on annual appropriations and on contracts that customers may end for convenience, recovering only the costs incurred and profit on work done.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 9, 10; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation F05; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit link is direct: stable, cost-protected cash flow supports debt service and refinancing confidence, while concentration in one buyer means a funding lapse reaches revenue at once, as the shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security from February to April 2026 showed. A government shutdown also cut fiscal 2026 revenue by about USD 26 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SAIC is listed on Nasdaq with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named, so creditors have no sponsor to inject equity and no sponsor to extract it. The credit facility is secured on substantially all assets and guaranteed by each wholly owned domestic subsidiary, and the notes due November 2033 are unsecured and guaranteed by the same subsidiaries. Financial policy is set by the board: dividends and buybacks may be limited at leverage ratios that are not printed, and governance risk is Medium because returns absorb most free cash flow and an antitrust investigation is open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 64, 132, 134; calculation F05; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by volume on existing contracts and new awards, with little price lever: contracts generally provide labour on a reimbursable basis and cost-type contracts pass costs through. Revenue fell 2.90% in fiscal 2026 on contract completions and ramp-downs, including the shutdown effect, and was about 3.3% lower excluding SilverEdge; it grew 3.84% in the first half of fiscal 2027, of which about 2.9% was organic and 5.3% in the second quarter alone. Revenue is concentrated, regulated and budget-cyclical rather than economically cyclical, and renewal of task orders each year refreshes bookings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 33; calculation F05; calculation F07; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Visibility is partial. Backlog of USD 22,136 million is 2.99 times last-twelve-months revenue, but only 17.25% is funded, net bookings were 0.88 times revenue in fiscal 2025, 1.07 times in fiscal 2026 and 0.87 times in the first half, and the company says greater use of competitive multi-award contracts and small-business set-asides has raised pricing pressure and reduced the addressable market. The implication is that revenue growth must come from winning work, not from pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 34; calculation F05; calculation F10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly labour and pass-through: in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 the labour base was 28.19% of revenue, other operating expenses, mainly subcontractors and materials, 61.65%, and adjusted operating income 10.16%, while in fiscal 2026 cost of revenues was 87.99% of revenue and operating income 7.17%. With cost-reimbursement contracts at 61.76% of revenue, inflation risk is limited, and the company says inflation has not had a significant effect in three years; the margin risk sits in the 15.75% of fixed-price work and in contract mix.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 91; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation F05; calculation F11; calculation F12; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are improving but the pace is slowing. Last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA margin is 10.55%, the first quarter was 11.6% against 8.4% a year earlier, and the second quarter slipped to 10.3% from 10.5% despite organic revenue growth of about 5.3%. Operating leverage is low because costs follow volume, so margins can be defended under volume pressure on cost-type work, but a mix shift toward fixed price or a decline in volume would lower them first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-01_saic.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 31; calculation F09; calculation F07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is minimal: capital expenditure was 0.44% of revenue in fiscal 2026, so there is little capital flexibility to find but also little need. Free cash flow of USD 577 million was 85.36% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and USD 619 million over the last twelve months, equal to 24.91% of gross debt, which is sizeable relative to debt on these definitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation F05; calculation F04; calculation F18; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conversion is helped by items that can reverse: receivables collections of USD 161 million in fiscal 2026 and cash taxes of USD 22 million against USD 66 million a year earlier, while receivables absorbed cash in the first half of fiscal 2027. Sales of receivables sit inside operating cash flow, so the facility, raised to USD 400 million after the quarter end, can move cash between periods without changing debt. The durable level of free cash flow is therefore below the reported peak and is not quantified in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 129; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20; calculation F04; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is intense and raises pricing pressure. Large defense primes, technical services peers and diversified commercial providers all compete, sole-source awards are fewer, and multi-award vehicles increase competition, which caps margins on re-competes and makes bookings the key indicator.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is moderate. Security clearances held by most of the workforce and past performance protect incumbents, but other-transaction agreements lower barriers to entry and small-business set-asides reduce the addressable market, so share loss is a gradual, not sudden, risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is very high. One buyer provides 97% to 98% of revenue, it may terminate contracts for convenience and it funds work by annual appropriation, so any adverse change in budgets or contract priorities reaches volume directly; cost recovery on terminated work softens the loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate and sits in labour. Cleared talent is scarce and competitors recruit aggressively, and subcontractors can fail to perform, but cost-type contracts pass wage and subcontract costs through, so the exposure is mainly on fixed-price work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings describe no substitute for outsourced government services; the substitution-like risk is the government reducing or reviewing contracts, which is covered under buyer power.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are the primary credit driver: appropriations, shutdowns, continuing resolutions, executive orders and agency contract reviews set volume, and the company's own statement is that it has not seen a material financial effect from recent orders or cancellations. Economic factors are secondary but real on the liability side: 63.99% of principal floats, so rates matter more than inflation, which cost-type contracts largely absorb. Social and technological factors are not primary drivers; demand for digital modernization, cyber and AI services is an opportunity rather than a risk to repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are federal revenue with cost-type protection, light capital needs, free cash flow of 24.91% of gross debt, a USD 1,000 million undrawn revolver and maturities of only USD 48 million through fiscal 2028. Weaknesses are one dominant customer, a backlog that is mostly unfunded, net debt rising with returns that absorb free cash flow, and no reported covenant ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F18; calculation F03; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The opportunities that could improve credit quality are demand for digital modernization, cyber and AI services and organic growth of about 5.3% in the second quarter, which would help deleveraging only if returns were held below free cash flow. Threats are a funding lapse, contract reviews and set-asides that reduce volume, the open antitrust investigation, and the refinancing of USD 400 million of notes due April 2028 at a time when gross leverage is 3.29x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 24, 27; calculation F07; calculation F01; calculation F03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is cash-flow durability: cost-reimbursement contracts carry 61.76% of revenue and capital expenditure is 0.44% of revenue, so most cost increases are passed through and free cash flow of USD 577 million covered debt service in fiscal 2026. The second is liquidity and maturity shape: USD 1,126 million of liquidity against USD 48 million of maturities through fiscal 2028 means no refinancing is needed before the notes due April 2028. The third is customer longevity: several relationships of 20 years or more and a USD 22,136 million backlog support renewal of work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 93, 115; calculation F05; calculation F03; calculation F16; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is shareholder returns that absorb free cash flow, 89.25% in fiscal 2026 and 128.11% in the first half of fiscal 2027, which with the acquisition lifted net debt by USD 141 million and USD 54 million with no sponsor or covenant ratio to restrain them. The second is dependence on one buyer, with 52.02% of revenue from the Department of War and 17.25% of backlog funded, so a funding or contract-review shock cuts volume. The third is fading momentum: second-quarter adjusted EBITDA rose 4.32% against 24.02% reported for the half, and net bookings were 0.87 times revenue. The fourth is an unquantified antitrust investigation and floating-rate exposure of 63.99% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 31, 34; calculation F04; calculation F05; calculation F06; calculation F10; calculation F13; calculation F02; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, cost-type revenue and cash generation. Scale is a strength: revenue of USD 7,402 million over the last twelve months is a large base for a services contractor, and free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because costs follow volume and capital needs are 0.44% of revenue, and margin stability is average, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 10.55% but a slip to 10.3% in the second quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation F02; calculation F18; calculation F05; calculation F09; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The constraints are concentration, financial policy and visibility. Business diversification is weak, because one buyer provides 97% to 98% of revenue and the Department of War 52.02%; competitive advantage is average, resting on 20-year relationships and clearances against rising price pressure. Free cash flow stability is average, since conversion of 85.36% in fiscal 2026 leans on receivables collections and low cash taxes. Financial policy and governance is average: reporting and audit quality are sound and returns are discretionary, but returns of 89.25% and 128.11% of free cash flow are not restrained by a sponsor or a printed covenant ratio, which is why governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-30_saic.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation F05; calculation F04; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance and access markets is average: the revolver and term loan A run to September 2030 and USD 400 million of notes fall due in April 2028, but no rating or market quote is supplied, so access is judged from the maturity profile alone. Liquidity is a strength at USD 1,126 million, before the dividend payable on 2026-10-23 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established. The trend is stable on adjusted leverage and rising on net debt, which was USD 2,359 million, or USD 2,374.5 million pro forma for that dividend; the missing datapoints are the covenant ratio, interim cash interest, any rating and evidence after 2026-08-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_saic.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation F03; calculation F01; Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is stable with a bias to slower earnings growth. Tailwinds are USD 6.4 billion of remaining performance obligations, 75% of which the company expects to recognise within twelve months, organic growth of about 5.3% in the second quarter and low capital needs. Headwinds are net bookings of 0.87 times revenue, a margin that slipped in the second quarter, a rise in term loan A amortisation from USD 27.50 million to USD 55.00 million a year from 2027-10-31, and a federal year that started after the filings end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outlook turns on refinancing and payout choices rather than on operations. Maturities are USD 48 million through fiscal 2028, then USD 489 million in fiscal 2029, USD 88 million in fiscal 2030 and USD 899 million in fiscal 2031, so the notes due April 2028 and the term loan A balloon are the tests; gross leverage of 3.29x is below the 3.68x at which the company ended fiscal 2026, after refinancing in September 2025, but each USD 100 million of returns funded by debt adds 0.13x. Sector tailwinds are spending packages for digital modernization and cyber; sector headwinds are shutdowns, continuing resolutions, contract reviews and set-asides, and the company says it is well positioned, which is management language and not evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a funding lapse or an agency contract review that cuts volume while shareholder returns continue. The first operational break would be delayed or stopped work on civilian and defense programs, as in the shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security from February to April 2026 and the shutdown that cut fiscal 2026 revenue by about USD 26 million; backlog is 17.25% funded, so most future work depends on later funding. Revenue and EBITDA would fall, but with 61.76% of revenue cost-reimbursed the margin falls less than volume, and the exposure is concentrated in the 15.75% of fixed-price work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial transmission is arithmetic. If last-twelve-months EBITDA returned to the fiscal 2026 level of USD 676 million, a fall of 10.58%, gross leverage would be 3.68x, the same as at the end of fiscal 2026, and if returns continued at the first-half level of USD 319 million while free cash flow fell, net debt would rise faster, with each USD 100 million adding 0.13x. Liquidity of USD 1,126 million is 23.46 times maturities through fiscal 2028, so liquidity distress is not in prospect; the lever is the board's choice to cut buybacks, which were USD 445 million in fiscal 2026, and the dividend, which was USD 70 million. A refinancing of the April 2028 notes at leverage of 3.68x is the first financing consequence; the covenant effect is not established because the ratio is not reported. An adverse result in the antitrust investigation, including debarment, would be a separate and larger break and is not sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, SAIC presents an adequate business profile supported by cost-reimbursed federal revenue, light capital needs and a seasoned customer base, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on one buyer, a mostly unfunded backlog, and shareholder returns that absorb most free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow of USD 619 million is 24.91% of gross debt, although conversion is flattered by receivables collections and low cash taxes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings momentum, which slowed in the second quarter, and on whether the board keeps returns below free cash flow before the notes due April 2028.

fields.value: The primary downside path is a funding lapse or contract review that cuts volume while returns continue to lift net debt. The profile is not benchmarked against typical leveraged-credit issuers because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant ratio, the proxy statement, interim cash interest, any rating, and evidence after 2026-08-31. Fundamental credit is complete. Top risk: shareholder returns that absorb free cash flow while one customer funds the business.
